messages:
pager-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED @oncall to #incidents — GPU pool 'g-prod-1' util 98%, queue depth 48k, autoscaler at max_nodes=24 (no further scale). ticket=INC-3332
oncall: ACK. seeing lots of 503s and p99 spikes to ~18s for text-gen endpoints. marking incident live.
marta: I deployed config change at 10:04 UTC — continuous-batching: batch_window_ms 12 -> 80 and prefix_cache_ttl 300s -> 30s (PR #4521).
samir: that batch_window jump would increase batch latency but also reduce effective batching frequency. curious why queue grew, not shrank. pulling autoscaler logs now.
infra-bot: metrics snapshot: gpu_util=0.98, queue_depth=48234, prefix_cache_miss_rate=0.87 (was 0.12 pre-deploy), eviction_rate=0.92. autoscaler: current_nodes=24, max_nodes=24, pending_scale=0.
jess: can we throttle non-prod tenants or route lower-cost model variants temporarily?
marta: rolling back the batch_window change now — doing a config rollback to previous batching profile (rollback-id=rb-4521). deploy-bot: starting rollback (cfg rollback-id=rb-4521)
samir: while rollback is in flight, we should open emergency capacity if possible. redwoodctl pool resize --pool g-prod-1 --count 30 (manual increase). I'll kick that.
infra-bot: command issued: redwoodctl pool resize --pool g-prod-1 --count 30 — accepted, provisioning GPUs (ETA ~3m).
olivia: applying request-level throttles for customers tagged 'dev' and 'low-priority' to 50% until further notice. route rule: /v1/generate -> route.lowpri=throttle:0.5
oncall: also toggling prefix cache warm-up to aggressive mode to rebuild hot prefixes: cachectl set warmup --pool g-prod-1 --mode aggressive
deploy-bot: rollback completed (rb-4521). batching.batch_window_ms=12, prefix_cache_ttl=300s.
infra-bot: after rollback + pool resize: queue_depth 48k -> 9.8k in 4m, gpu_util 98% -> 86%, prefix_cache_miss_rate 0.87 -> 0.18, p99 latency 18s -> 2.6s, 503 rate back to baseline.
jess: good — still keep throttles in place for 20m while we validate.
marta: confirmed root cause: the recent change aggressively reduced prefix cache TTL and increased batch window; short TTL caused cache churn and high miss pressure, larger batch window increased queuing latency and prevented effective throughput smoothing. combination produced queue growth and pushed autoscaler to its cap.
samir: follow-ups: 1) revert batch_window change permanently until we simulate with spike tests; 2) add autoscaler soft cap alerts earlier (notify at 80% of max_nodes); 3) add canary gating for cache TTL changes.
oncall: customer impact: approx 14 tenants saw elevated errors (5% of active tenants), one enterprise customer (ACME Inc) hit sustained 5xx for ~7m, CS notified. No data loss.
jess: tagging for postmortem, assigning action items. SRE to own autoscaler alert tuning (samir), product to own safer rollout for batching/cache (marta), support to contact impacted customers (olivia).
oncall: incident mitigated at 10:35 UTC. closing page but keeping thread open for postmortem notes. (reaction :thumbsup:)
